events.title: Anne Boleyn Is Executed
events.description: Anne Boleyn, the second wife of King Henry VIII, was beheaded at the Tower of London. She had been convicted of treason, adultery and incest on charges that most historians regard as fabricated.
events.significance: Her fall reshaped the Tudor court. Her daughter, Elizabeth I, later became one of England's most celebrated monarchs.

events.title: Atatürk Lands in Samsun
events.description: Mustafa Kemal landed at the Black Sea port of Samsun. The Ottoman government had sent him to restore order in Anatolia, and he used the post to organize resistance to the Allied occupation.
events.significance: This landing is traditionally taken as the start of the Turkish War of Independence. It led to the founding of the Republic of Turkey in 1923, and Turkey marks the day each year as a national holiday.

events.title: Malcolm X Is Born
events.description: Malcolm Little was born in Omaha, Nebraska. He later became known as Malcolm X, a minister and activist.
events.significance: He became one of the most influential voices in the American civil rights era. His speeches and his autobiography still shape discussions of race, identity and justice.

events.title: Marilyn Monroe Sings 'Happy Birthday, Mr. President'
events.description: At a Madison Square Garden fundraiser, Marilyn Monroe performed a breathy rendition of 'Happy Birthday' for President John F. Kennedy, who was turning 45.
events.significance: The performance became one of the best-known moments in American pop culture. It remains one of the most famous images of celebrity and politics meeting.
